title: Third reel: managers and leaders of the Owls
summary: The third reel begins and Frank explains Earl Crum managed the Owls, nobody led, and who could read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I think I got a lot of things I want to ask you. We've got the third reel on Frank Netto,
and it's the 10th of November, 1986. Who were the leaders and managers of the Owls through the years?

Earl Crum was the manager. Leader? I don't think there was any leader. They just put the music out there on the stand and they went along and if they did any improvising they did it as a group to go along there, but they didn't read too well. You agree with me, Godfrey? Yeah. Sieg Christensen, when he joined the band, he read fairly well and Dan LeBlanc read fairly well. He was the tuba player and Bill read a little bit, trumpet player and Pinky didn't read that well, but Benji White, he carried the sax section. While Pinky didn't read too well, he was a mediocre reader as far as musicianship was going. But he standing up there in the front with a baton, but he couldn't handle his shoulder.
